newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan govt to mull extra spending after data -- EPA.
newsitem.headline: Japan govt to mull extra spending after data -- EPA.

text.p: The government will decide if extra fiscal spending is necessary to maintain Japan's economic recovery after looking at key data, Economic Planning Agency (EPA) Minister Shusei Tanaka told a news conference on Tuesday.

He said the Bank of Japan's "tankan" survey of corporate sentiment due out on Wednesday and gross domestic product data for the April-June quarter, expected next month, were the focus of much attention.

But he said he had not changed his stance that the government should not easily rely on fiscal spending. Rather, now was the time to push for structural reform, in particular deregulation, to help the recovery continue, he said.
Tanaka said there was more concern about the economic outlook for fiscal 1997/98, starting next April, than for the current year, as a rise in the consumption tax was due to take place in April.
He said, however, there was room for debate on steps such as continuing special tax cuts after the release of the tankan and GDP data.
